lines.trans: Do they trick all newcomers like that?
I must quickly put on my chef's hat.
Chef, today is the fifteenth, do you remember?
Soon the restaurant's sanitary inspection will arrive.
And in your kitchen there is a mess again!
Where do you see a mess, my dear?
Look for yourself what a clean shelf this is!
A little money solves any big problems.
If there were order, we wouldn't pay!
There is always a lot of work in a restaurant kitchen.
Inspectors look for violations only for money.
We must urgently establish perfect cleanliness.
It seems today we have big problems.
I will go wash the floors in the kitchen.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
We have a bit of a mess here.
There was total chaos in the room.

examples.text: Извините, у нас тут небольшой бардак.
examples.trans: Excuse us, we have a bit of a mess here.

meanings.note: Privative prefix 'бес-' ('without, -less', before voiceless consonants) (stem 'порядок'). Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'disorder, disturbance' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: To cause disturbances on the street.
There is complete disorder in the room.

examples.text: Он устроил беспорядки прямо на городской улице.
examples.trans: He caused disturbances right on the city street.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('big, large').

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.

meanings.note: with a past-tense verb: я бы подумал = I would think
wishes: купили бы = we could have bought

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
present есть; у меня есть = I have

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.
I can see the toy car.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.
She was running after me (around me).
She circled around me like a shark.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'егда').

examples.trans: She's offended. She's always like that.

examples.text: Решается ваш вопрос, Клавдия Викторовна! Вы не видите, у меня встреча?
examples.trans: Your question is being sorted out, Klavdia Viktorovna! Can't you see I have a meeting?

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?
examples.trans: Hey, where's the toy car? Where's my toy car?

meanings.note: plural only: there is no singular in everyday use

examples.trans: The money is on the table.
Gum? I didn't have enough money.

meanings.note: to a loved one, and at the start of letters
to a loved one, and at the start of letters

examples.text: В Москве вам дают деньги на дорогую одежду, а мозги не дают.
examples.trans: In Moscow they give you money for expensive clothes, but they don't give you brains.

meanings.note: condition: если хочешь = if you want; а если нет? = and if not?

examples.text: Мы создадим идеальную команду для работы.
examples.trans: We will create an ideal team for work.

examples.text: Сегодня стояла идеальная погода для прогулки.
examples.trans: Today there was ideal weather for a walk.
For ideal order in the universe.

examples.text: Инспекторы ищут нарушения только ради денег.
examples.trans: Inspectors look for violations only for money.
The inspector is checking the kitchen.

meanings.note: International noun in '-ция' (from Latin '-tio'), feminine declension. Common feminine noun meaning 'inspection' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Soon the sanitary inspection will arrive.
This is a strict rule of the sanitary inspection.
Soon the restaurant's sanitary inspection will arrive.

meanings.note: Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'кать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to look for'.

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: мне кажется = I think, it seems to me

examples.trans: I think I've seen you somewhere.

meanings.note: in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'chef's hat, cap' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The chef put on a white hat.
The chef wears a white chef's hat.

examples.text: Я съем колпак, если мои повара уйдут!
examples.trans: I will eat my chef's hat if my cooks leave!
Three rooms and a big kitchen.
And the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: в любой момент = at any moment

examples.text: Любая обезьяна эти выборы выиграет! Ты что, хуже обезьяны?
examples.trans: Any monkey will win this election! What, are you worse than a monkey?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('small, little').

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

examples.text: Юля, встала и пошла мыть посуду!
examples.trans: Yulia, get up and go wash the dishes!

examples.text: Пока ещё на мои деньги куплен! Встала и мыть посуду, шагом марш!
examples.trans: It's still bought with my money! Get up and wash the dishes, forward march!
The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.
I will establish iron order here.

examples.text: Дежурный офицер навёл идеальный порядок в части.
examples.trans: The duty officer established ideal order in the unit.

examples.text: Да, я наведу здесь железный порядок.
examples.trans: Yes, I will establish iron order here.

meanings.en: to put on (an item of clothing)

examples.trans: He put on his best suit.

examples.text: Карамельно-сливочный цвет. Очень тебе к лицу! Надень куртку.
examples.trans: A caramel-cream colour. It really suits you! Put the jacket on.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary

examples.trans: We need to do even more.
That is a violation of the law.

examples.text: Свидетель обвинения надёжный. Нарушений я не нашёл.
examples.trans: The prosecution witness is reliable. I found no errors.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.text: Говорят, что всем новичкам всегда везёт.
examples.trans: They say that all beginners always get lucky.

examples.text: Ты шутишь, шеф никогда не берёт новичков!
examples.trans: You are joking, the chef never takes novices!

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'манывать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to deceive, to cheat', paired with 'обмануть'.

examples.text: Потому что она простая. Её все обманывают.
examples.trans: Because she's naive. Everybody cheats her.

meanings.note: Core Russian pron meaning 'they' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

examples.text: Нина, не слушай. Это опять обман.
examples.trans: Nina, don't listen. It's another trick.

meanings.note: платить за + accusative = to pay for

examples.text: А вашу работу вернуть можно. И мы хорошо платим.
examples.trans: But we can get your job back for you. And we pay well.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'варской'). Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('chef's, culinary').

examples.trans: The chef's hat is lying on the table.
The chef put on a chef's hat.
I will eat my chef's hat!
Can I go and have a look?

examples.text: Возьми хорошую бутылку на верхней полке.
examples.trans: Take a good bottle on the top shelf.

examples.text: А теперь внимательно посмотри на эту полку.
examples.trans: And now look carefully at this shelf.

examples.text: Мы проверили все столы и полки.
examples.trans: We checked all tables and shelves.
Do you remember the toilet in the communal flat?

meanings.note: по порядку = in order; всё в порядке = everything is fine

examples.trans: Now let's go through everything in order.

examples.text: Теперь давай всё по порядку. Скажи мне, сколько ты им должна?
examples.trans: Now let's go through everything in order. Tell me, how much do you owe them?

meanings.en: to have a look, to take a look

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?
Security will be here any moment.

examples.text: Не надо, Самсон. Сейчас придёт охрана.
examples.trans: Don't, Samson. Security will be here any second.
I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('fifteenth').

examples.text: Сегодня пятнадцатое число, большая санитарная проверка!
examples.trans: Today is the fifteenth, a big sanitary inspection!

examples.text: Шеф, сегодня пятнадцатое число, ты помнишь?
examples.trans: Chef, today is the fifteenth, do you remember?
Work, work. It's all for us.

examples.text: Слушай, Нина, это же тот самый ресторан!
examples.trans: Listen, Nina, this is that very restaurant!

examples.text: Мы рады видеть вас в нашем ресторане.
examples.trans: We are glad to see you in our restaurant.
They called from the Italian restaurant.

meanings.en: to decide, to make up one's mind

examples.trans: Decide for yourselves what to do.

examples.text: Вот он, телефон! Сами решайте, что делать. Без меня!
examples.trans: Here it is, the phone! Decide for yourselves what to do. Without me!

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

examples.text: Сегодня пятнадцатое число, большая санитарная проверка!
examples.trans: Today is the fifteenth, a big sanitary inspection!
This is a strict rule of the sanitary inspection.

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: comparative of скоро used as adverb or particle

examples.trans: Let's go quickly to the studio!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'коро'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Так, не шумим. Я скоро вернусь.
examples.trans: Right, no noise. I'll be back soon.

meanings.en: urgently, right away; predicative: it is urgent
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'рочно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I need to make a phone call urgently.

examples.text: Павел Юрьевич, это срочно! Я должна вам сказать.
examples.trans: Pavel Yuryevich, this is urgent! I must tell you.

meanings.note: at the start of a question

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'number, date' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Сегодня пятнадцатое число, большая санитарная проверка!
examples.trans: Today is the fifteenth, a big sanitary inspection!

examples.text: Шеф, сегодня пятнадцатое число, ты помнишь?
examples.trans: Chef, today is the fifteenth, do you remember?

examples.text: У меня здесь всегда полная чистота.
examples.trans: I always have complete cleanliness here.
We must urgently establish perfect cleanliness.

examples.text: Да, шеф требует идеальной чистоты везде.
examples.trans: Yes, Chef demands perfect cleanliness everywhere.

meanings.note: short form чисто: всё чисто = everything is clean

examples.text: Нин, я всё помыл. Всё чисто.
examples.trans: Nina, I washed everything. It's all clean.

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
